title: Encrypted DNS Discovery RFC 9463 DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR Wire Verification
verification_method: Focused unit tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, DNS package build, full solution test, and diff hygiene for the RFC 9463 DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR wire surface.
scope: This verification covers OPTION_V4_DNR tag and length fields, DNR Instance Data length and field order, RFC 8415 authentication-domain-name wire formatting, IPv4 Addr Length and address-list encoding, public and private IPv4 address support, RFC 9460 SvcParams encoding and alpn preference, default port lookup when the port SvcParam is absent, computed SvcParams field length, ADN-only mode field omission, RFC 3396 segmentation for oversized option data, Parameter Request List data, multiple DNR instances, service-priority ordering, invalid-instance discard, and loopback/multicast address discard behavior.
preconditions: The RFC 9463 specification exists as canonical JSON at `specs/requirements/quic/SPEC-QUIC-RFC9463.json`.
DHCPv4 wire support remains a pure option codec and does not implement a platform DHCP client.
expected_result: The focused DHCPv4 option tests pass, the DNS package builds, core SpecTrace validation accepts the RFC 9463 artifacts, generated triage reflects the DHCPv4 wire slice, diff hygiene passes, and the full solution test suite remains green.
status_summary: The RFC 9463 DHCPv4 OPTION_V4_DNR wire floor is trace-owned and verified. Neighbor Discovery, PKIX validation, and resolver installation remain future work.
